headline: Recommends National Register listing for the Harvey Gammage, a schooner docked at 100 West Commercial Street.
summary: The meeting covered a National Register nomination for the Harvey Gammage, a wood schooner built in 1973. Members voted 5-0 to recommend it to the Maine Historic Preservation Commission. A workshop on a nine-townhouse project at 101 and 105 Winter Street drew feedback, but no vote was taken.
decisions: Recommended that the Maine Historic Preservation Commission support listing the Harvey Gammage on the National Register of Historic Places, 5-0.
discussion: Harvey Gammage nomination: Members said the vessel's 1973 construction and training role fit the National Register criteria A and C, and no one spoke against it.
Winter Street townhomes: Members discussed the long second-floor facade, the large window sizes, and how visible building B is from the street, and asked for more study before a public hearing.
Winter Street public comment: Speakers praised the project's scale and details, and one suggested keeping the facade's rhythm instead of grouping the end units.

decision_evidence.quote: I'll move to recommend the main historic preservation commission support the nomination for the Harvey gomage, docked at 100 West Commercial Street ... Motion carries. All present in favor.

decision_titles: National Register nomination for the Harvey Gammage
